title: Indian Families Pay Millions to Escape H-1B Trap
excerpt: A $100,000 H-1B fee and a 20-year green card backlog are pushing Indian professionals toward the EB-5 investor visa as a last resort.
body:
A seismic shift is reshaping how Indian professionals chase permanence in America. After President Trump signed a proclamation on September 19, 2025, imposing a $100,000 fee on all new H-1B petitions, Indian families are pooling savings, liquidating investments, and pivoting to the EB-5 investor visa — an immigration route that once belonged firmly to the ultra-wealthy.

**What changed — and how much it costs:**
USCIS confirmed that the $100,000 payment must accompany every new H-1B petition filed after September 21, 2025, a 20-fold jump from the previous ceiling of roughly $5,000. The fee applies to foreign nationals outside the United States seeking a new visa. Immigration attorneys now warn that H-1B workers who lose their jobs face a 60-day grace period — after which they too may trigger the six-figure requirement if they seek re-entry from abroad.

**Why Indian families are turning to EB-5:**
India accounts for 71% of all H-1B visa recipients, per USCIS data, making the community the most exposed to the change. With EB-2 green card backlogs stretching beyond 20 years for Indian nationals, immigration advisors report families assembling close to $1 million in pooled assets to qualify for the EB-5 program. The EB-5 investor visa requires a minimum of $800,000 invested in a USCIS-approved targeted employment area project and the creation of 10 full-time U.S. jobs. India's Ministry of External Affairs called the H-1B overhaul likely to produce 'humanitarian consequences by way of the disruption caused for families,' urging Washington to act.

**What to watch:**
The Department of Labor is drafting new rules to raise prevailing wage floors for H-1B holders, a second wave of reform that could further narrow who qualifies — and force more families to weigh the investor-visa gamble before those EB-5 rural set-aside backlogs, currently moving fastest, close entirely.
